tasks.short: Document patient histories and diagnostic information

steps.what: Clarify the patient's actual history, symptoms and physical condition, distinguishing the patient's account from observed findings.
inputs: Actual patient account and examination findings
outputs: Actual clarified clinical facts and uncertainties

steps.what: Capture the actual encounter facts by clinician dictation in the clinical record workspace {OTHER}, including pertinent negatives and unresolved questions.
Write the patient's history, symptoms, physical conditions and other diagnostic information as a draft clinical note in {OTHER}.

loop.purpose: Draft a clinical narrative from the midwife's actual dictation
loop.input: Permitted encounter dictation from s2 and existing headings
loop.output: Source-linked note draft with uncertainties preserved
loop.check: Midwife verifies actual meaning, attribution, negation, timing and omissions in s5
loop.stop: One draft and one correction, then manual writing; no orders, diagnosis or sending tools
loop.why_not_simpler: Native headings are used first, but the actual clinical account is narrative and cannot be composed by literal field copying.

steps.what: Transfer already measured vital signs and available test results from their verified source records into the clinical-note draft {OTHER} using native record links.
inputs: Existing measured results with patient and encounter identifiers
outputs: Complete note draft with traceable measured results

steps.what: Verify and correct the complete note against the actual patient account, examination and source results, preserving uncertainty and correcting clinically important omissions.
Save the actual encounter note in the same clinical record {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Test native clinical-note templates and result links in {OTHER} first. A permitted bounded drafting loop can compose the narrative from actual clinician dictation; the midwife still captures the facts and verifies the complete clinical meaning before ordinary internal storage.
tasks.previous_blocker: Narrative writing and repeated result entry can interrupt documentation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record links and bounded prose drafting can produce a traceable draft without making care decisions.
tasks.still_hard: Negation, timing and an omitted clinical concern can change the meaning of the note.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish what the patient reported, what was observed and what remains uncertain.

ambition.what: Return documentation time to the actual clinical encounter.

tasks.altitude: Less first-draft writing; clinical accountability and note validation remain.

reach.learn: Audit source provenance and clinically significant omissions without changing clinical conclusions.

build_days.consent_and_access: 5-15 for health-data safeguards, permitted model processing and national consultation where applicable

evidence.claim: Clinical narrative drafts can be produced from actual clinician input and verified by that clinician; result links can replace manual repeated entry.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual history clarification, explicit dictation capture, narrative writing, existing-result transfer and complete note validation. No ambient recording or free transcript is assumed.

The midwife produces actual narrative input in s2. Existing measurement staff/instruments and laboratory records already produce patient id, encounter id, observation code, value, unit, timestamp and validity flag; their collection time stays unchanged and earns no saving. Unmatched records are manually entered and checked, not inferred.

Conditional E1 activity shares for a manual note-writing and result-re-key scenario. Existing automatic result links earn no saving. Native templates are tested first; if model processing is not permitted, narrative writing stays manual. Routine same-system saving has no separate approval stage and is fully retained.
unknowns: Which result transfers are still manual?
Can the permitted record system support a restricted drafting service?
research_questions: Does the draft preserve negation, attribution and temporal relationships without adding unsupported clinical statements?

already_counted.description: Actual encounter clarification, dictated capture, draft review, clinical correction and storage

incremental.description: Audit note omissions and recheck templates and result mappings after updates

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 35*0.35 + 10 = 22.25; minus 2 upkeep gives 20.25, high rounded down to 20.2. Conservative case: the record already links results and the narrative has ambiguities requiring full rewriting; retain the existing documentation method rather than adopt drafting. Capture and clinical validation remain in both cases.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prescribe within the midwife's permitted scope

steps.what: Review the actual patient history, pregnancy context, current medicines, allergies and available relevant findings in the clinical record {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual current patient record and encounter findings

steps.what: Decide whether and what to prescribe within the midwife's actual national professional scope, weighing benefits, risks and alternatives.
inputs: Actual patient preferences and clinical assessment

steps.what: Enter the actual prescribed medicine, directions and patient/prescriber fields in the electronic prescribing workspace {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual medication and directions from s2

steps.what: Review the existing medication-surveillance warnings against the actual order and patient, investigating clinically relevant interactions or contraindications.
Explain the actual proposed medicine and directions to the patient and address questions and concerns.
inputs: Actual proposed prescription and reviewed warnings from s3-s4
outputs: Patient discussion and any required order changes

steps.what: Resolve any changes in {OTHER} and clinically authorise the complete final prescription only after rechecking the exact patient, medicine, directions and destination.
outputs: Complete final prescription v1 and practitioner authorisation

steps.what: Transmit only the final practitioner-authorised prescription through the existing prescribing exchange {OTHER}.
inputs: Final authorised prescription v1 from s6
outputs: Prescription transmitted to the specified destination

tasks.design: Use native patient and practitioner field reuse in the electronic prescribing workspace {OTHER}. The midwife chooses the treatment, reviews existing surveillance, counsels the patient and clinically authorises the completed prescription before the separate transmission; no AI prescribes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated administrative identifiers can be re-entered during order composition.
tasks.enabler_now: Native order entry can reuse verified encounter and practitioner fields.
tasks.still_hard: A technically complete order may still be inappropriate for the actual patient or outside professional scope.
tasks.human_edge: Make and explain the accountable clinical prescribing decision.

ambition.what: Preserve clinical decision and counselling time.

tasks.altitude: No prescribing authority changes; only repeated field entry is reduced.

reach.learn: Communicate clinical context and resolve prescription queries within professional scope.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-7 for prescribing permissions and clinical governance

evidence.claim: Native order-entry field reuse can reduce repeated identifiers; professional prescribing and warning review remain clinical work.

assumptions: State regulations in the task are interpreted as actual national prescribing scope; this makes no claim about a particular country's permissions. Only an appropriately authorised practitioner prescribes.

Patient and practitioner records already supply verified identifiers and encounter context; s2 supplies the actual clinical choice. s3 reduces only repeated administrative fields. Missing identifiers require manual verification; no medication or direction is inferred.

Conditional E1 shares, with all existing native surveillance runtime excluded from labour savings. s6 is actual professional prescribing authorisation, not an invented self-approval for an ordinary save. Any change to v1 voids authorisation and requires fresh clinical review before s7. Transmission stays 1% fully retained.
unknowns: What is the midwife's actual authorised scope?
Are administrative fields already reused natively?
research_questions: Can repeated identifiers be reused without copying stale patient context or changing the clinician-selected order?

already_counted.description: Clinical assessment, order review, warning interpretation, counselling and professional authorisation

incremental.description: Check reused identifier fields after prescribing-system changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed prescription v1, including destination, clinically authorised at the end of s6; any change voids it

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only 15*0.20 = 3 gross points from repeated identifiers; minus 0.5 upkeep gives 2.5. Conservative case: the current prescribing system already populates these fields, so keep it unchanged. No benefit is claimed from existing surveillance, clinical decisions or transmission runtime.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and implement individualized care plans

steps.what: Discuss the patient's actual health needs, preferences, circumstances and available support.
Locate the current care information and relevant approved pathway in the clinical record {OTHER}.
inputs: Current clinical record and approved care pathways

steps.what: Develop the individualized health care management plan with the patient, deciding appropriate actions, responsibilities, follow-up and escalation within professional scope.
Write the actual individualized plan in the clinical record {OTHER}, using native headings and repeated patient/encounter fields.
Implement the agreed care activities and coordinate directly with the patient and care team, observing the actual response.
inputs: Actual patient condition and care-team involvement
outputs: Actual care implementation and observed response

steps.what: Record the actual care activities, response and any plan changes in {OTHER} after implementation.
inputs: Actual implementation and response from s5

steps.what: Save the actual care-plan and implementation record in the same clinical workspace {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual care record from s4 and s6

tasks.design: Configure native pathway navigation and care-plan headings in {OTHER}. The midwife develops the actual individualized plan with the patient, writes its clinical content, implements care and records actual outcomes; no template chooses treatment or marks future care complete.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding pathway context and repeating document fields can interrupt planning.
tasks.enabler_now: Native care-plan views and verified encounter fields can reduce those small administrative parts.
tasks.still_hard: Patient preferences, changing condition and practical support determine a workable plan.
tasks.human_edge: Agree a plan that is clinically appropriate and feasible for this patient.

ambition.what: Keep more of the planning encounter available for patient preferences.

tasks.altitude: No new clinical decision rights; less navigation and header entry.

reach.learn: Make responsibilities and observed care responses clear at handoff.

build_days.consent_and_access: 2-5 for clinical records and template governance

evidence.claim: Native care-plan headings and encounter-field reuse can assist documentation while individualized clinical planning remains human.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual patient discussion, plan creation, written plan, implementation and post-care record. Separate referrals or prescription orders, where needed, retain their own professional authorisation process; no saving is claimed for them here.

The patient and midwife produce goals in s1 and actual plan choices in s3. Existing records supply verified patient id, encounter id and approved pathway version. Missing fields or unsuitable pathways require manual work; templates never supply care decisions.

Conditional E1 activity estimates. s4 changes only headings and repeated identifiers, retaining all actual clinical writing and checks. Native configuration comes first; the routine same-system save is fully retained and ungated.
research_questions: Can templates support a genuinely individualized plan without copying stale care actions?

already_counted.description: Actual patient goals, pathway checks, clinical planning, writing, implementation and outcome capture

incremental.description: Check pathway versions and repeated-field accuracy

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 2 navigation plus 1.5 headings/identifiers = 3.5; minus 0.5 upkeep gives 3. Conservative case: the plan needs a nonstandard pathway and the current record already supplies headings, leaving full navigation and clinical writing retained with no new configuration.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain procedures to patients and others

steps.what: Locate the current approved information for the actual procedure in the clinical information collection {DOCS}.
Explain the actual procedure to the patient, family or staff, adapting to understanding and language needs and checking questions and comprehension.
Write the actual explanation, questions and unresolved concerns in the clinical encounter note {OTHER}.
inputs: Actual explanation and understanding checks from s2

steps.what: Save the actual explanation note in the same clinical record {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Use native procedure and language filters in the approved {DOCS} collection. Explanation and comprehension checks stay with the midwife, and the actual encounter note is written separately; no automatic patient message or consent inference is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Occasional approved-source lookup can interrupt explanation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native filters can find the approved procedure page more directly.
tasks.still_hard: A patient can repeat words without understanding their implications.
tasks.human_edge: Respond sensitively to fear, uncertainty and actual understanding.

ambition.what: Protect the human explanation rather than shorten it.

tasks.altitude: The conversation and clinical responsibility do not change.

reach.learn: Use teach-back and arrange appropriate communication support.

evidence.claim: Approved information filters can reduce source lookup but do not replace patient-specific explanation.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual procedure explanation and its separate encounter record. No new handout-writing, consent approval or message-send baseline is added.

Existing information owners provide procedure id, approved language version, revision and source link. The midwife supplies the actual procedure and communication needs; absent or unsuitable material is handled manually, never generated as personal clinical advice.
Conditional E1 shares. Only a small source lookup changes; the 85-share conversation and new note content are fully retained. Native filters are tested first; ordinary saving has no gate or saving.
unknowns: Is procedure material already immediately accessible?
research_questions: Can the midwife find the approved language version without confusing information access with actual patient understanding?

already_counted.description: Relevant-source check, actual explanation, comprehension checks and note writing

incremental.description: Check approved procedure-page links after revisions

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Gross 1 minus 0.2 upkeep gives 0.8. Conservative case: the procedure is familiar and no material lookup is needed, or its approved page is already immediately accessible; retain the present explanation and record process without adopting an extra filter.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Less repeated documentation work while keeping patient conversations, individualized care and professional prescribing decisions.
reach: Improve record traceability with medical records specialists
role.ambitious_version: A midwife with more attention available for the patient and clear, accurate care records.
